stem:
Kim is a 10-year-old girl who has been using salbutamol (Ventolin) and budesonide (Pulmicort) 50 micrograms BD. While at asthma camp, she used her counsellor’s orange puffer twice a day after her own puffer fell in the swimming pool. The counsellor was taking fluticasone (Flixotide).

You tell Kim’s parents that the puffer that Kim was using at camp contained a medication that is:

options.text: Less potent than budesonide, therefore she was probably receiving less steroid dose
Equipotent to budesonide, therefore she was probably receiving the same steroid dose
More potent than budesonide, therefore she was probably receiving more steroid dose
Irrelevant - there is no relationship between the steroid dose of different medications

explanation: Fluticasone is a more potent inhaled corticosteroid than budesonide. If Kim used the same nominal microgram dose, she was likely receiving a greater corticosteroid effect than from her usual budesonide dose.

citations.title: Practice Quiz: Asthma Management: Medications and Devices - Part A

optionExplanations.A: Incorrect. Fluticasone is not less potent than budesonide.
optionExplanations.B: Incorrect. These inhaled corticosteroids are not equipotent on a microgram-for-microgram basis.
optionExplanations.C: Correct. Fluticasone is more potent than budesonide, so the same puff dose would deliver a greater steroid effect.
optionExplanations.D: Incorrect. There is a clear potency relationship between different inhaled corticosteroids.
